target_customer: Developers building chatbots and language interfaces; later government and defense customers
problem: Chatbots rely on brittle keyword matching; Plasticity offered APIs that parse sentences into entities and relationships.
business_model: Usage based NLP APIs, later software and services for government

founders.name: Alex Sands
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says product and engineering at those companies. TechCrunch says the founders built a hack adding voice commands to Siri.

founders.name: Ajay Patel
founders.background_notes: YC page lists a personal site but no background.

competitors.name: Google
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch named Google the main competitor

competitors.name: IBM Watson
competitors.traction_then: Plasticity claimed higher accuracy and speed than Watson at parsing

technical_complexity.rationale: Deep learning semantic parsing trained on Wikipedia, more than 1.5 years of development per TechCrunch, is research adjacent for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Large players offered free or cheap NLP and the approach was only run over Wikipedia at launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Big platforms commoditized NLP APIs; Plasticity pivoted to government and was bought by EX1 in October 2020.

market_need_then: The 2016 and 2017 chatbot wave created demand for better language understanding; TechCrunch reported the APIs moving from private to public beta in August 2017.

branding.domain_note: Used plasticity.ai, an AI top level domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Site headline Machines that comprehend language; API names Sapien, Cortex and Lingua

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch once; the name is shared with an unrelated design tool and other companies.

pivots.to: Government and Department of Defense work
pivots.why: One directory source says commercial sales stalled; not confirmed by a primary source

outcome_analysis: Plasticity launched NLP APIs after YC in 2017 against Google and IBM, raised an undisclosed seed from Dorm Room Fund and Rough Draft Ventures, and drifted toward government work. EX1 acquired it on October 16, 2020 for undisclosed terms and kept it as a subsidiary. The sale looks modest and no stated cause is public, so the failure factors are inferences.
notes: The website is live and now sells to government and commercial customers, with a Disinformation Toolkit. CB Insights snippet reports 340K total from NSF, YC and Dorm Room Fund, unverified so not recorded as rounds. Seed amount unknown. Failure factors and the pivot cause come from a directory source plus inference. YC page says the batch is Summer 2017 and the company is based in San Francisco.
